If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, shift forecast downward by 1–2% to reflect sentiment reversal.

For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains positive but price has already peaked, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for mid-horizon to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for mid-horizon to avoid underestimating decline.
